item.title: Didactic Audiovisual Translation (DAT)
item.description: Didactic audiovisual translation – or DAT – is a flourishing research field within audiovisual translation (AVT). Publications in this area have surged since the 2010s, and the interdisciplinary nature of the field has been enhanced through collaborative efforts among researchers in translation studies, applied linguistics, and education. item.title: Perceptions of Audio Introduction by the Blind and Partially Sighted Audiences in Iran
item.description: Audiovisual Translation (AVT) advocates for further access to multimedia content for individuals with special needs. Audio Description (AD) and Audio Introduction (AI) tools serve to facilitate the engagement of Blind and Partially Sighted (BPS) individuals with these contents, contributing to media accessibility. item.title: Exploring the Role of Agency in the Production of Easy Subtitles
item.description: This study investigates the role of human agency in creating easy subtitles, or subtitles written in Easy-to-Read language (E2R) for audiences with reading difficulties. Grounded in media accessibility and cognitive psychology, it explores the audience interaction with easy subtitles and whether their comprehension is affected by the source language of the audiovisual material. item.title: A Different Fate of Two Dubbed Versions of a Film
item.description: This article explores how translation recontextualizes films for different national audiences, focusing on the contrasting fates of Five Fingers of Death and its Korean-dubbed version of Iron Man. By conducting a historical analysis of both the English and Korean dubbed versions, the study shows how the transnational journey of the film has influenced the development of these two versions. item.title: The Informal Ukrainian Voiceover
item.description: This article offers the first ever introduction to the practice of informal Ukrainian voiceover translation of fiction. Specifically, it outlines the defining traits of this voiceover style, such as the presence of multiple voices and isochrony, and how it compares to the more widely known voiceover techniques.
